description: Choline-containing compound used as a supplemental source of choline and as a precursor for acetylcholine-related signaling.
used_for: Brain health; cognitive decline support; exercise power output.
benefits: May support cognitive symptoms in people with cognitive decline and may acutely improve power output in some exercise contexts.
how_it_works: Alpha-GPC is broken down largely into choline, which the body can use to make acetylcholine and phospholipids involved in nerve signaling and cell membranes.
recommended_dosage: For cognitive-decline contexts, studies commonly use 1200 mg/day split into 3 doses of 400 mg. For power output, 300-600 mg has been studied before exercise.
recommended_timing: For performance use, 30-60 minutes before exercise; for cognitive protocols, split across the day.
bioavailability_notes: Largely absorbed as choline; monitor total choline exposure when stacking with other choline sources.
clinical_description: Generally well tolerated, but possible GI upset, headache, restlessness, and theoretical cardiovascular caution due to TMAO-related concerns.

description: Adaptogenic herb, most often supplied as a root extract, used traditionally in Ayurveda and now commonly used for stress and wellbeing support.
used_for: Stress; anxiety; sleep; physical performance; reproductive health.
benefits: May reduce perceived stress and anxiety, may modestly support sleep and some performance or testosterone-related outcomes, though effects vary by extract and dose.
how_it_works: Likely acts through multiple pathways, including stress-response regulation, neurotransmission, inflammation/oxidative-stress modulation, and withanolide-related activity.
recommended_dosage: Common research range is 150-600 mg/day of root extract, often split into 1-3 doses. Studies have used wider ranges, but higher dosing is not clearly better.
recommended_timing: Flexible; many protocols take it daily with food. Some traditional use pairs it with milk or ghee, though superiority is not established.
bioavailability_notes: Extracts vary widely in withanolide content and formulation, so product standardization matters.
clinical_description: Usually tolerated but may cause drowsiness or GI symptoms. Avoid in pregnancy/lactation; use caution with thyroid issues, liver concerns, autoimmune conditions, organ transplant history, or immunosuppressive drugs.
notes: Paraphrased from Examine trial extraction; educational only.

description: Plant alkaloid used in traditional medicine systems and commonly researched for glucose and lipid metabolism.
used_for: Blood glucose management; type 2 diabetes support; lipid management; PCOS-related metabolic support.
benefits: May lower fasting glucose, improve some insulin-resistance markers, and support blood lipid improvements in some populations.
how_it_works: Appears to influence cellular energy and metabolic signaling, including AMPK-related pathways, glucose handling, gut microbiome effects, and lipid metabolism.
recommended_dosage: 900-2000 mg/day total, divided into 3-4 doses to improve tolerability.
recommended_timing: With or shortly after meals, especially meals likely to raise blood glucose and lipids.
bioavailability_notes: Divided dosing is important because larger single doses are more likely to cause GI upset.
clinical_description: GI cramping, stomach upset, or diarrhea can occur. Use medical caution with diabetes medications, pregnancy/lactation, and complex medication plans.
notes: Paraphrased from Examine trial extraction; educational only.

description: Amino acid used to raise muscle carnosine, mainly for repeated high-intensity exercise performance.
used_for: High-intensity exercise; muscular endurance; training performance lasting roughly 1-10 minutes.
benefits: Can improve performance in hard efforts where acid buildup limits output, especially repeated or sustained high-intensity work.
how_it_works: Beta-alanine combines with histidine to form carnosine in muscle; carnosine helps buffer hydrogen ions during intense exercise.
recommended_dosage: 3.2-6.4 g/day has been used effectively. A common loading approach is 4-6 g/day split into doses of 2 g or less for at least 2-4 weeks.
recommended_timing: Timing is not critical; split doses across the day to reduce tingling. Sustained-release forms may allow larger doses.
bioavailability_notes: Taking with meals containing carbohydrate and protein may help carnosine loading, but timing matters less than daily consistency.
clinical_description: Main side effect is paresthesia/tingling, especially at higher single doses. Limited pregnancy/lactation safety data; caution with glucose-lowering medications.
notes: Paraphrased from Examine trial extraction; educational only.

description: Synthetic peptide investigated for regenerative and tissue-repair effects; current human evidence is very limited.
used_for: Experimental gut health and tissue-repair interest only; not a routine supplement recommendation.
benefits: Animal studies suggest possible tissue-protective and regenerative effects, but there is little reliable evidence of meaningful benefits in humans.
how_it_works: Mechanisms remain uncertain in humans; animal work suggests effects on healing pathways, blood vessel formation, inflammation, and tissue-protective signaling.
recommended_dosage: No established human dose. Examine lists only an animal-to-human estimate from rat oral data: about 1.6 mcg/kg, roughly 110 mcg for 150 lb, 145 mcg for 200 lb, or 180 mcg for 250 lb; this is not a validated human recommendation.
recommended_timing: No reliable timing guidance for human use.
bioavailability_notes: Human pharmacokinetic data is lacking, and many products are sold for research purposes rather than approved human use.
clinical_description: High caution: not approved for human use by major regulators, safety data is limited, and it is prohibited at all times by WADA.
notes: Not recommended as a standard client supplement without medical oversight; row retained for database completeness.
